findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it private within the VPC.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage and snapshots, leaving database data unprotected at rest.
The master password is supplied from var.password in plaintext Terraform input and is written to state; combined with the default 'admin' username this makes credential compromise likely.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so only static password authentication protects the database; no IAM-based auth or rotation is available.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general logs) and Performance Insights encryption are configured, so database access cannot be audited after a compromise.

The user_data script interpolates the database master password (var.password) and username into a shell script; user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service (IMDSv1 by default) and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking DB credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 is permitted and any SSRF or local code execution on the web server can steal the instance profile credentials and the user-data secrets.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's EBS volume (which stores the credential file written by user data) may be unencrypted at rest.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing any compromise of the web server to read/modify all S3 data, launch or terminate EC2 instances, and manipulate every RDS database in the account.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on every protocol and port, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised database host.

The database security group has no description and relies on separate rules; combined with publicly_accessible = true on the RDS instance, the VPC-scoped ingress rule is the only control preventing internet reach to port 3306.
The database endpoint is emitted as an unmarked Terraform output, disclosing the publicly accessible DB hostname to anyone able to read state or CI logs.
